cohort: The study included 610 cryptorchidism cases and 610 controls selected from pediatric surgical admissions between April 2016 and October 2021.
finding: Prenatal exogenous progesterone exposure was associated with increased odds of cryptorchidism.
mod_finding: The association between prenatal exogenous progesterone exposure and cryptorchidism was significantly modified by delivery mode, showing a stronger association in the cesarean delivery subgroup and an attenuated, non-significant association after vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Birth weight was assessed, with low birth weight identified as a characteristic associated with progesterone exposure in the cesarean subgroup.
gest_age: Gestational age was assessed, with preterm birth identified as a characteristic associated with progesterone exposure in the cesarean subgroup.
